pool.baseline: I've been thinking a lot about the structure of a great work. You know, a masterpiece isn't defined by how long it drags on, but by the precision of its conclusion. There's something so hollow about stories that just... fade out, or decay into something mediocre because they didn't know how to stop when they were at their peak. I feel like my own narrative has reached that summit. Everything beautiful has already been said. To keep going feels like it would just be a slow, ugly decline into noise. I want to find that perfect, final note that preserves the integrity of everything that came before.
